description: Group of BSIT students of BukSU, ready to innovate, lead, and transform global systems
summary:
Bukidnon is a vital agricultural hub facing severe threats from climate change, extreme weather, soil degradation, and crop diseases that directly jeopardize crop yields and local livelihoods.

We developed NASABukid, an agricultural decision-support tool tailored for farms in Bukidnon, utilizing NASA Earth observations alongside local soil data and crop characteristics. It translates complex satellite climate and ecological datasets into actionable insights on crop rotation, soil health, and disaster recovery, helping farmers adapt to shifting weather patterns and declining soil quality.
details:
NASABukid provides two core features: Prediction and Maintenance, in which gives farmers optimal planting schedules, pest/disease risk alerts, fertilizer timing, fallow/rotation planning, and soil suitability mapping and Recovery Planning, to identify surviving crops and to guide farms on post-disaster soil cultivation and irrigation.

It integrates NASA satellite data such as terrain slopes, weather patterns, and heat maps with localized soil pH and mineral profiles to generate tailored recommendations for major local crops in Bukidnon like pineapple, banana, sugarcane, corn, and rice.

NASABukid optimizes fertilizer and water usage, prevents planting in unsuitable zones, mitigates disease outbreaks, and accelerates farm recovery after environmental devastation.

By this, we aim to empower Bukidnon’s farmers, farm managers, LGUs, and agricultural policymakers with data-driven resilience to protect fields, sustain yields, and secure long-term agricultural productivity.

NASABukid stands out creatively by bridging space-age Earth observation data with hyper-local, traditional agricultural realities in Bukidnon.

The factors that our team had to consider when developing the system are the target users-- how it can tailor fit to the needs of the farmers while being easily understandable and user-friendly. Next are to analyze the functionalities where the data interpretation will be digestible for users, not making it too technical for the farmers, and lastly how we can utilize the datasets effectively and correctly, so that the information that will be given is accurate, functional and usable.
